kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-01.title: Order by size
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-01.body:
The mushroom gets bigger every day, so put the photos from smallest to biggest mushroom:

- smallest: photo 2
- then photo 5
- then photo 3
- then photo 1
- biggest: photo 4

That gives 2-5-3-1-4.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-01.title: Check the ends first
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-01.body:
The first photo must show the smallest mushroom (photo 2) and the last one the biggest (photo 4). Only (A) starts with 2 and ends with 4.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-02.title: Compare each tile
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-02.body:
Look at the wall: each tile is a square with coloured petals in its corners and edges. Find each candidate tile in the wall (you may need to turn it). Tiles (A), (B), (C) and (E) each appear in the wall. Tile (D) has two orange petals on top and a pink shape at the bottom next to green — no square of the wall looks like that.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-02.title: Use the colours
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-02.body:
In the wall, the green corners always meet orange petals on the left and right and pink pieces only meet each other in pink 'stars'. In tile (D) a pink petal sits next to green in a way that never happens in the wall, so it cannot be part of it.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-03.title: Calculate every square
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-03.body:
- $28-4=24$ ✔
- $4\times 6=24$ ✔
- $18+6=24$ ✔
- $19+6=25$ ✘
- $8\times 3=24$ ✔
- $29-6=23$ ✘

So the whole top row is painted and only the middle square of the bottom row.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-03.title: Bottom row only
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-03.body:
The top row: $28-4$, $4\times6$ and $18+6$ are all 24, so all three are painted — that rules out (B) and (E). In the bottom row only $8\times 3 = 24$ (the middle). The picture with a full top row and only the bottom middle painted is (C).

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-04.title: Look for a piece that is not there
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-04.body:
The pieces are: a blue stick, a small red triangle, a yellow triangle, a blue triangle, a pink circle and a green circle. Picture (C) contains a red **square**, which is not one of the pieces.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-04.title: Count the pieces
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-04.body:
Every picture should use exactly the six pieces: 2 circles, 3 triangles and 1 stick. (A), (B), (D) and (E) do. (C) has a red square instead of the small red triangle.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-05.title: List the numbers
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-05.body:
Starting at 1 and adding 3 each time, Eli writes nine numbers:

1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25.

From the choices only 10 and 22 are in the list, and 10 is already written in another square. So the coloured square could hold **22**.

**Answer: (E) 22**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-05.title: Remainders
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-05.body:
Every number Eli writes is 1 more than a multiple of 3 (1, 4, 7, ...). Among the choices, 10 and 22 have this property (14, 17, 20 do not). Since 10 is already on the board, the answer is 22.

**Answer: (E) 22**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-06.title: Count the layers
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-06.body:
A hole punched through folded paper makes one hole in **every layer** of paper at that spot.

- The first fold (the two top corners) puts 2 layers near the nose.
- The second fold folds the slanted edges in again: 4 layers there.
- Folding the plane in half doubles it once more: 8 layers.

The hole goes through 8 layers, so after unfolding there are **8 holes**.

**Answer: (D) 8**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-06.title: Unfold step by step
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-06.body:
Undo the folds one at a time. Each time you unfold, every hole gets a mirror copy on the other side of the fold: 1 hole → 2 → 4 → 8 after the three folds that pass over the nose of the plane.

**Answer: (D) 8**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-07.title: Count each tray
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-07.body:
Three quarters means 3 out of every 4 squares.

- A: 4 squares, 3 coloured ✔
- B: 12 squares, 9 coloured ✔
- C: 16 squares, only 8 coloured — that is one half ✘
- D: 8 squares, 6 coloured ✔
- E: 16 squares, 12 coloured ✔

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-07.title: Look at the white squares
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-07.body:
If three quarters are coloured, one quarter is white. In C the white and coloured squares alternate like a chessboard, so half of the squares are white — far more than a quarter.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-08.title: Find the possible rectangles
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-08.body:
The pieces are strips of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 squares, so together they have $1+2+\dots+7 = 28$ squares. A rectangle of 28 squares can be $1\times 28$, $2\times 14$ or $4\times 7$ (the strip of 7 has to fit, so $7\times 4$ is the same shape).

All three can be built:

- $1\times 28$: put all strips in a row.
- $4\times 7$: rows $7$, $6+1$, $5+2$, $4+3$.
- $2\times 14$: rows $7+6+1$ and $5+4+3+2$.

Their perimeters are 58, 32 and 22: **3** different perimeters.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-08.title: Why not more?
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-08.body:
The area is always 28, and the only ways to write 28 as width × length are $1\times28$, $2\times14$, $4\times7$. Each gives a different perimeter, and each can be made, so there are exactly 3.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-09.title: Top cube of each column
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-09.body:
From above you only see the **top** cube of each stack, so each square shows the colour of the highest cube standing on it. Go along the construction: the tall stacks have light cubes on top, and the dark cubes are only seen where nothing stands on them. Comparing square by square, only picture (B) has the light and dark squares in the right places.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-09.title: Eliminate
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-09.body:
Count the columns of the construction: it has squares in two rows of the grid. Pictures that show squares in the wrong rows, or show a dark top where a light cube sits on top, can be crossed out. (A), (C), (D) and (E) each have at least one such mistake; (B) is left.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-10.title: Each region touches the two before it
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-10.body:
Look at the regions from the outside in: the outer ring, then a band at the top, a band at the bottom, a band at the top, ... down to the small oval in the middle. Each region touches the region just before it **and** the one before that.

- The outer ring: 3 choices.
- The next region touches it: 2 choices.
- The third region touches both: only 1 colour left.
- Every later region touches the two previous ones, which have two different colours, so its colour is forced.

Total: $3\times 2\times 1 = 6$.

**Answer: (E) 6**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-10.title: The colours just repeat
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-10.body:
Once the first three regions are coloured, say red, blue, yellow, the rest must continue red, blue, yellow, red, ... So a colouring is decided by the order of the three colours, and three colours can be ordered in $3\times2\times1 = 6$ ways.

**Answer: (E) 6**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-11.title: Go around both ways
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-11.body:
The rope is tied on the 7 m side, 1 m from the corner on the right.

- **To the left:** it takes $7-1 = 6$ m to reach the top-left corner, leaving $11-6=5$ m. That is exactly the length of the left side, so the dog can reach the bone on the left side and the bottom-left corner.
- **To the right:** 1 m to the top-right corner, then 5 m down to the bottom-right corner, leaving $11-6 = 5$ m along the bottom side. That reaches the three bones in the middle of the bottom side.

The bone at the bottom-left corner is reached by going down the left side. So the dog can get all **5** bones.

**Answer: (E) 5**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-11.title: Mark what the rope covers
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-11.body:
Walk along the fence from the tying point and mark how far 11 m gets you.

- Left way: the 6 m of the top side + the whole 5 m left side.
- Right way: 1 m + the whole 5 m right side + 5 m of the 7 m bottom side.

The only part of the fence the dog cannot reach is a short piece of the bottom side near the left corner, and no bone lies there (the corner bone is reached down the left side). All 5 bones can be eaten.

**Answer: (E) 5**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-12.title: Use the posts
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-12.body:
There are 5 upright pieces (posts), each half a metre wide. Each long horizontal piece (2 m) reaches from the left edge of one post to the right edge of the next post. So from the left edge of one post to the left edge of the next is $2 - 0.5 = 1.5$ m.

From the first post to the fifth there are 4 such steps: $4\times 1.5 = 6$ m, plus the width of the last post, $0.5$ m.

Length $= 6.5$ m.

**Answer: (B) 6.5**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-12.title: Add the horizontal pieces
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-12.body:
The four horizontal pieces go from post 1 to post 2 (top), post 2 to post 3 (bottom), post 3 to post 4 (top) and post 4 to post 5 (bottom). Laid end to end they would measure $4\times 2 = 8$ m, but neighbouring pieces share the width of posts 2, 3 and 4, half a metre each. Length $= 8 - 3\times 0.5 = 6.5$ m.

**Answer: (B) 6.5**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-13.title: Follow the pattern around the crown
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-13.body:
Each piece touches its two neighbours with one triangle each, and between those two triangles there is one triangle on the inside of the crown.

Start with the bottom piece and go to the right. The bottom piece touches its left neighbour with **1**, has **5** inside and touches its right neighbour with **4**. The next piece then touches with 4, has 3 inside and touches the next with 2; the next touches with 2, has 1 inside and passes on 5; and so on. The numbers go down by one each time, so after **5** pieces the pattern repeats.

With 10 pieces, the piece opposite any piece (5 pieces further) is exactly the same piece turned half way round. The coloured triangle belongs to the piece opposite the grey piece just right of the bottom one, and sits where that grey piece has its **1** (on the outside, at the far corner).

**Answer: (A) 1**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-13.title: Half a turn
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-13.body:
Turn the picture upside down: the crown looks the same, because the pattern of pieces repeats every 5 pieces and 10 is twice 5. The coloured triangle then lands on the outer triangle of the grey piece to the right of the bottom piece, which shows the number 1.

**Answer: (A) 1**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-14.title: Opposite faces
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-14.body:
When the net is folded: the 1 (top square) is opposite the 4 (bottom square), the 6 (left) is opposite the 2 (the square right of the centre), and the 3 (centre) is opposite the 5 (far right).

Opposite faces can never be seen together:

- (C) shows 1 and 4 — impossible.
- (D) shows 5 and 3 — impossible.
- (E) shows 2 and 6 — impossible.

(A) and (B) both show 4, 5/2 and 2/3. In the net, the two dots of the 2 run from the corner next to the 3 and the 1 to the corner next to the 4 and the 5. In (A) the 2 is drawn exactly like that. In (B) the dots of the 3 point to the wrong corners. So only (A) works.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-14.title: Fold it in your head
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-14.body:
Put the centre square (3) in front, 1 on top, 4 at the bottom, 6 on the left, 2 on the right and 5 at the back. Now turn the cube forward twice so that 4 comes on top: then 5 is in front and 2 is on the right — exactly cube (A).

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-15.title: Count the jumps
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-15.body:
The kangaroo starts at the bottom (step 0) and the rabbit on step 100. To reach step 56 the kangaroo makes $56 \div 7 = 8$ moves of 7 steps. During those moves the rabbit goes down $8\times 3 = 24$ steps: $100 - 24 = 76$.

**Answer: (B) 76**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-16.title: Find what each had
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-16.body:
Ana had twice as much as Bia and twice as much as Cris, so Bia and Cris had the same amount. If Bia had 1 part, Cris had 1 part and Ana 2 parts: 4 parts = 100 reais, so Bia and Cris had 25 each and Ana 50.

Try the ticket prices: with 20 reais, Ana has 30 left and the friends have 5 + 5 = 10. And $30 = 3\times 10$ ✔.

**Answer: (E) R\$ 20.00**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-16.title: Check all choices
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-16.body:
Ana had 50, Bia 25, Cris 25. After paying a ticket price $t$: Ana has $50-t$, the friends together $50-2t$.

- $t=8$: 42 vs 34
- $t=10$: 40 vs 30
- $t=12$: 38 vs 26
- $t=15$: 35 vs 20
- $t=20$: 30 vs 10 → three times ✔

**Answer: (E) R\$ 20.00**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-17.title: Count the front flowers
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-17.body:
On the front of the left cactus we see 7 flowers, so it has $7+3 = 10$ flowers in total. The right cactus has $10+6 = 16$ flowers. On its front we see 4 flowers, so on its back there are $16 - 4 = 12$.

**Answer: (D) 12**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-17.title: Compare directly
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-17.body:
The right cactus has 6 more flowers in total, but on the front it shows $7-4 = 3$ fewer. So on the back it must have $3 + 6 = 9$ more than the left cactus: $3 + 9 = 12$.

**Answer: (D) 12**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-18.title: Size of each piece
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-18.body:
The grid has $16 - 1 = 15$ squares, so each piece has 5 squares. Every option has 5 squares, so we have to find which shape can cover the grid three times.

Shape (A) works: label rows 1 (top, with 3 squares) to 4.

- Piece 1: the 3 squares of row 1 and the first 2 squares of row 2.
- Piece 2: the last 2 squares of rows 2 and 3, and the last square of row 4.
- Piece 3: the first 2 squares of row 3 and the first 3 squares of row 4.

All three are copies of (A).

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-18.title: Rule out the others
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-18.body:
The corner square next to the missing square can only be covered in a few ways. The cross (E) and the long shapes (C), (D) cannot fit three times into a $4\times4$ square with a missing corner, and three copies of (B) (a U shape) leave holes. Only (A) works, as shown in the first solution.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-19.title: Roll it step by step
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-19.body:
At the start: top 1, front 2, right 3, so bottom 6, back 5, left 4.

1. Roll right: the top goes to the right side. Top 4, right 1, front 2.
2. Roll right again: top 6, right 4, left 3, front 2.
3. Roll forward (towards us): the top goes to the front. Front 6, top 5, right 4.
4. Roll right: top 3, right 5, front 6.
5. Roll right: top 2, right 3, front 6.

The coloured faces (front and right) show 6 and 3: $6\times 3 = 18$.

**Answer: (D) 18**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-19.title: Two rolls in a row
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-19.body:
Rolling twice in the same direction turns the die upside down in that direction: top and bottom swap, and the two sides in that direction swap. The two rolls right make the top 6. Rolling forward sends that 6 to the front, where it stays for the last two rolls to the right. Those two rolls swap left and right: before them the left side was 3 (opposite the 4 on the right), so at the end the right side is 3. Product: $6\times3 = 18$.

**Answer: (D) 18**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-20.title: What day does each one say it is?
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-20.body:
- Adam: yesterday Wednesday → today Thursday.
- Beto: tomorrow Friday → today Thursday.
- Carlos: the day before yesterday Tuesday → today Thursday.
- David: the day after tomorrow Saturday → today Thursday.
- Eli: today Monday.

Four friends agree that today is Thursday, so Eli was wrong.

**Answer: (E) Eli**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-20.title: Only one is wrong
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-20.body:
If Eli were right (Monday), then Adam, Beto, Carlos and David would all be wrong — but only one person is wrong. So Eli is the one.

**Answer: (E) Eli**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-21.title: Use the total
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-21.body:
$1+2+\dots+8 = 36$. The triangles and the squares have the same sum, and the circle is a quarter of that sum. So the total is made of 4 quarters (triangles) + 4 quarters (squares) + 1 quarter (circle) = 9 quarters. $36 \div 9 = 4$, so the circle covers **4** and the triangles add up to $4\times 4 = 16$.

Triangles + circle $= 16 + 4 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-21.title: Try values for the circle
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-21.body:
If the circle is $c$, the triangles and squares each sum to $4c$, so $c + 4c + 4c = 9c = 36$, giving $c = 4$. (For example: triangles 1, 2, 5, 8 and squares 3, 6, 7.) Triangles + circle $= 16 + 4 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-22.title: Choose the wing first
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-22.body:
The wing can be any of 3 colours. Then the head can be either of the other 2 colours, and the tail also either of those 2 colours (it may match the head). That gives $3\times 2\times 2 = 12$ different parrots.

**Answer: (D) 12**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-22.title: List for one wing colour
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-22.body:
If the wing is red, head and tail are chosen from blue and green: (blue, blue), (blue, green), (green, blue), (green, green) — 4 ways. The same holds for a blue or a green wing: $3 \times 4 = 12$.

**Answer: (D) 12**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-23.title: Look at Jonas
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-23.body:
Both had ice cream on each of the same days. Jonas ate at most 3 scoops a day. In 7 days he could eat at most $7\times3 = 21 < 23$ scoops, so they needed at least 8 days.

In 8 days it works: Jonas $7\times 3 + 1 \times 2 = 23$, Elias $3\times 3 + 5\times 2 = 19$.

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-23.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-23.body:
6 or 7 days are too few for Jonas (at most 18 or 21 scoops). For 8 days, Jonas can eat between 16 and 24 scoops and Elias too, and both 23 and 19 are in that range. So 8 days is the least.

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-24.title: Which codes can be read two ways?
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-24.body:
A confusing code must have 3 digits and be readable both as *one-digit floor + two-digit room* and as *two-digit floor + one-digit room*.

Write the code as $a\,b\,c$.

- Floor $a$, room $bc$: the room is 10–20, so $b = 1$ (or $bc = 20$).
- Floor $ab$, room $c$: the room is 1–9, so $c \neq 0$, and the floor $ab$ is at most 30.

So $b = 1$, $c$ is 1 to 9, and $ab$ is 11 or 21 (31 is too high): $a$ is 1 or 2. That gives $2 \times 9 = 18$ codes: 111–119 and 211–219.

**Answer: (E) 18**

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-24.title: List them
kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-24.body:
Floor 1 with rooms 11–19 gives codes 111, ..., 119, which could also be floor 11 with rooms 1–9. Floor 2 with rooms 11–19 gives 211, ..., 219, which could also be floor 21 with rooms 1–9. Floor 3 with room 11 gives 311, but there is no floor 31. Room 20 ends in 0 and no room is numbered 0. Total $9+9 = 18$.

**Answer: (E) 18**
